title: Default recursive test discovery is not a native filesystem operation
observed_need: Find independent manifests across a repository while keeping discovery deterministic and inspectable.
current_language_behavior: MNCS does not currently expose portable recursive directory enumeration to an external consumer, but the compiler now discovers first-class tests structurally within an explicit source/module target.
why_insufficient: Project-root and compatibility-manifest enumeration still needs a bounded host/package boundary; recursive source scanning is neither required nor used for ordinary test declaration discovery.
minimal_reproducer: tools/mncs_test.py: discover_manifests(root, recursive=True) uses sorted os.walk/rglob only when explicitly requested; run invokes mncs test-inventory for each named source.
desired_direction: A package/module-aware native discovery contract, or a bounded standard-library directory enumeration API with stable ordering and capability grants.
workaround: The normal run path requires an explicit root manifest and direct tests/*.toml compatibility entries; recursive manifest discovery is opt-in and sorted, while runtime test names come from the compiler inventory.
